title: Semester and Recipe
premise: Ada Okafor has survived three years in the tiny town of Marrow Bend by being invisible — until the school's legendary ghost begins leaving her handwritten notes in ink that shifts color and can't be photographed. The notes lead her to a hidden archive proving the town's founding fortune was stolen from a Black family whose descendants still live nearby, and that the ghost is a student from decades ago who died protecting it. As Ada investigates, she discovers the 'ghost' is actually alive: an elderly custodian, Ruth Vance, who faked her death to keep watch over the evidence. When the school board moves to demolish the old wing — and with it the archive — Ada must choose between the safety of silence and exposing the truth at the spring talent show's final audition, where she publicly reads the founding documents aloud. The town convulses, the Okafor name becomes synonymous with justice, and Ada finally stops performing carefulness and starts living out loud.
about_author: Emrys Quintana is the pen name of a former small-town debate champion who now writes stories about kids who refuse to shrink. They live near a lake, keep a drawer full of unsent letters, and believe every haunted school deserves a second hearing.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes Marrow Bend, Ada's exhausting self-monitoring as the only out kid in town, and her plan to survive senior year unnoticed. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ada finds the first note in her locker — her full name in shimmering ink that vanishes when photographed. She assumes it's a cruel prank. POV Ada. Beat: fear sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Legend of Room 114
chapters.summary: Best friend Theo recounts the ghost story: a student who vanished in 1971 after a fire in the old wing. Ada notices details that don't match the official record. POV Ada. Beat: first crack in the town's tidy history.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: The ghost leaves a note quoting something Ada said only aloud, alone, in the empty auditorium. Terrified but hooked, she answers in pencil. POV Ada. Beat: the dangerous thrill of being truly seen.

chapters.title: What Devon Saw
chapters.summary: POV Devon, the principal's son and Ada's lab partner, who glimpsed someone in the old wing and is being pressured to stay quiet. His loyalty to his father wars with his conscience. Beat: complicity has a cost.

chapters.title: The Archive Behind the Chalkboard
chapters.summary: Following the ghost's clues, Ada finds a concealed room: decades of letters, ledgers, and photographs proving the Harlan family's land was seized to build the town's fortune. POV Ada. Beat: awe curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: Ada confronts the 'ghost' — Ruth Vance, the elderly night custodian, presumed dead since 1971. Ruth explains why she hid: the men who took the land would have destroyed the evidence, and her. POV Ruth. Beat: grief worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Harlan Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Ada tracks down Imani Harlan, a retired teacher living two towns over, who stopped believing anyone would listen. POV Ada. Beat: hope offered cautiously, like a hand across a table.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: A rumor about Ada and a girl from the next county spreads; her mother's fear and love collide at the kitchen table. POV Ada. Beat: the cost of visibility without power.

chapters.title: Devon's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Devon finds his father shredding old correspondence and realizes the family knows more than he thought. He copies one page before fleeing. POV Devon. Beat: the first act of open rebellion.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: The school board announces the old wing will be razed by June — conveniently destroying the archive. Ruth's health is failing; time is short. POV Ada. Beat: dread becoming urgency.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ada signs up for the spring talent show, planning to use her audition slot for something no one expects. Theo worries she'll make herself a target. POV Ada. Beat: resolve hardening against fear.

chapters.title: Imani's Testimony
chapters.summary: Imani visits the archive and recognizes her grandmother's handwriting; she agrees to go public if the documents are authenticated. POV Imani. Beat: inherited grief transformed into inherited claim.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Someone reports 'squatting' in the old wing; the police seal the door. Devon secretly passes Ada the page he copied — proof his grandfather signed the seizure order. POV Devon. Beat: betrayal of blood for what's right.

chapters.title: Cornered
chapters.summary: Principal Whitlock warns Ada about her 'obsession,' dangling a college recommendation letter. She realizes how far the town will go to protect its story. POV Ada. Beat: temptation of the quiet life.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: Hospitalized, Ruth tells Ada the full truth of the fire — she set it herself to hide the archive, and a classmate died in the chaos. Her guilt explains fifty years of hiding. POV Ruth. Beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Plan
chapters.summary: Ada, Theo, Devon, and Imani plan to authenticate copies and expose everything during the talent show, when the whole town is in one room. POV Ada. Beat: terror and purpose braided together.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: The show's faculty advisor cuts Ada's act; Devon's father threatens expulsion; the copied page goes missing. The plan seems dead. POV Devon. Beat: despair before the last stand.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Ada takes the stage anyway, uninvited, and reads the founding ledger aloud while Theo projects scanned pages and Imani stands beside her. The auditorium erupts. POV Ada. Beat: the climax — voice as verdict.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The demolition halts; a state investigation opens; Whitlock resigns. Not everyone forgives Ada — some friendships end — but the Harlan claim proceeds. POV Ada. Beat: victory that isn't clean.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Note
chapters.summary: Ruth, dying, gives Ada the final note: her real name, her real story, permission to tell it. The town buries her under her true identity. POV Ada. Beat: mourning joined to gratitude.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Graduation day. Ada walks the stage holding Imani's hand, no longer performing carefulness but choosing openness freely. A new note appears — this time she wrote it, for the next kid. POV Ada. Beat: inheritance passed forward.
